approved: Customs Legislation Amendment (Controlled Trials and Other Measures) Bill 2022
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would allow time-limited trials of new technology, business models and approaches in customs, with oversight, to inform future regulatory reform.
The Comptroller-General of Customs could make rules setting qualification criteria for entities to participate and rules for each specific trial, including its purpose, period and conditions.
Schedule 1 would commence on a day fixed by Proclamation or, if not within 6 months of Royal Assent, the day after that period; Schedule 2 would commence the day after Royal Assent.
The bill creates a new regulatory framework in Part XB of the Customs Act for controlled trials.
The bill allows the Comptroller-General of Customs to make general rules for qualification criteria and specific rules for each trial.
The bill defines 'controlled trial' and 'controlled trial provision' to limit trials to specified Parts of the Customs Act, excluding prohibited imports and exports.
The bill makes technical amendments to align customs legislation with current legislative practice.
The bill clarifies the operation of the Legislation Act 2003 regarding Notices of Intention to Propose Customs Tariff Alterations.
The bill amends the Australian Border Force Act 2015 to prevent delegation of the Comptroller-General of Customs' rule-making powers for controlled trials.
Entities approved to participate in controlled trials, the Comptroller-General of Customs, and the Australian Border Force.

The majority voted against [amendments](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Famend%2Fr6952_amend_f9863d76-1c13-4810-80e8-73b6db70d865%22;rec=0) introduced by West Australian Senator [Gordon Steele-John](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/wa/jordon_steele-john) (Greens), which means they failed. The amendments related to forced labour and would have introduced a prohibition on importing goods produced by forced labour.

The shadow minister for home affairs argued that the Customs Legislation Amendment (Controlled Trials and Other Measures) Bill 2022 is essentially the same as the coalition's previous bill, with trials limited to 18 months and the Comptroller-General of Customs having power to suspend or revoke approval with seven days' notice. He also criticised the government for gutting the Home Affairs portfolio and failing to back legislation on ransomware and Operation Sovereign Borders.
